children: The proposed investment will cover energy, transport and logistics, and businesses such as cement, copper and aluminium

The Adani Group plans to invest more than USD 120 billion in capital expenditure over the next five years across its infrastructure businesses and emerging growth platforms, according to an interview given by its executives to Fortune India on Tuesday.
The investment is expected to cover the group's businesses in energy, transport and logistics, as well as sectors such as cement, copper and aluminium.

"Over the next five years, we plan to invest about USD 120 billion — over USD 20 billion a year — across all our businesses," Pranav Adani, a director at the group's flagship firm Adani Enterprises and nephew of group chairman Gautam Adani, told Fortune India.

According to the report, around 70 per cent of the planned investment will be allocated to energy, 20 per cent to transport and logistics, and the remaining 10 per cent to business adjacencies, including cement, copper and aluminium.

The group estimates that the planned investments will help double its asset base to Rs 18 lakh crore (USD 191.64 billion) over five years. It also expects core earnings, measured as earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA), to reach between Rs 2.6 lakh crore and Rs 3 lakh crore during the period.
The Adani Group has businesses across ports, airports, power, renewable energy and other infrastructure sectors.
